recipes.name: Richard and Suzanne's Famous Spaghetti Sauce
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chilies, undrained

steps.text: Pour the olive oil into a skillet and place over medium heat. Cook the garlic in the hot oil 1 to 2 minutes; add the onion, bell pepper, basil, green onion, and bay leaf and cook until the bell pepper softens; season with salt and pepper. Stir in the tomato sauce, stewed tomatoes, diced tomatoes with chiles, water, and sugar; continue to cook 20 to 30 minutes, stirring every 5 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Richard and Suzanne's Famous Spaghetti Sauce
raw_recipe.description: We created this spaghetti sauce because my wife did not like thick sauce. Therefore, we came up with this recipe and have used it for over 20 years. We are always asked for the recipe, but, until now, had never given the recipe to anyone. Hope you enjoy!!

review.reviewBody: Wow, this receipe is the best non-thick Spaghetti Sauce we have ever tried. The sauce is great with pizza, dipping sauce, spaghetti, lasagna. You should bottle this up and sell it. We followed the recipe exactly and will never change it. Again, thanks!! Your crawfish recipe rocks too.

Loved this recipe and have gotten rave reviews from all who consumed. I made some slight modifications... 1.) I simmered for many hours 2.) I added water gradually, 1/2 cup at a time to achieve consitency I liked. 3.) Put stewed tomatos in the food processor prior to putting in the pan (because I can't eat chunks of tomatos) 4.) added some sliced sausage Thanks much for this great recipe!

This recipe is soooo good. My husband said he didn’t want to use bought spaghetti sauce any longer! I followed the recipe except I cut the sugar in half and since I put the sauce in the crock pot, I didn’t add the water- crock pot did that for me. Excellent taste. Not too thin, not too thick - just right.

DELICIOUS! My husband said this was as good as sauce from a fine Italian restaurant. I used yellow bell pepper instead of green because my husband hates green pepper, and I left out the water on the advice of other reviewers. It was a perfect consistency and the flavor was awesome. Look no further, this is GREAT sauce!

This sauce has an amazing flavor!!! I did not add the water as directed, used 1/2 the sugar and added about 1/2# diced fresh mushrooms. My boyfriend thinks I'm a gourmet cook and asked me to make a double batch next time. Thank you for sharing this wonderful recipe, Richard & Suzanne. I normally don't like tomato-based sauces for spaghetti (I use olive oil, basil & julienned sun-dried tomatoes) but this recipe has changed my opinion.

This was a good pasta sauce. It wasnt one of my favorites but I enjoyed making it. I dont like my sauce as thin as this recipe is, so I only added about 2 cups of water and simmered a lot longer, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours. I did have to season this very well with italian seasonings and dried basil. When putting in fresh basil at the beginning it pretty much mellows out the flavor and is better to add close to the end to get the full basil flavor. I chunked up some yellow squash and added it in as well. The sauce came out nice and robust from all the vegies and simmering longer. It didnt seem to coat the spaghetti as well as other pasta sauces do, and it made a big batch! So we had plenty of leftover sauce. Thanks for the recipe! I may make again sometime because I really liked the addition of all the vegies in it.

My family LOVES this sauce. I made a couple of small changes; I used crushed tomatoes instead of the tomato sauce (to make it just a bit chunkier), omitted the green pepper (because I'm the only one in my family of 4 who likes it) and added an extra can of Italian style diced tomatoes instead of the water because I didn't want the sauce to be too thin. It turned out fabulous! This is the 3rd time I'm making it this month!!! Thank you so much for sharing this recipe, it's perfect for the days I've forgotten to defrost meat for dinner and I always have all of the ingredients on hand!!

As an Italian we never put green peppers nor onions in our sauce. Instead of white sugar, brown sugar cuts the acidity much better. My grandmother who was the first in our family to be born in the USA, always used fresh chopped basil. Sparingly with Oregano, minced garlic, and always a smidge of creole seasoning for a fun kick, also known as Arrabbiata. We also always made sure there were homemade meatballs and a lot of ground beef in the sauce. We always season to the taste buds.
The sauce is very good, but far too thin. I think a two to three hour simmer would work far better than the 20 to 30 minutes in the recipe.
Excellent! Didn't add any water & only used about 1 tsp of sugar. This is a keeper. Thanks for the recipe!
great flavor but way too watery. I dont like it thick, but man! This is too too watery. Next time I will not add water.

I cook a lot and I also read a lot of recipes. I just assumed that this was a recipe for Italian tomato sauce. The bell pepper takes the recipe somewhere else. Latina? but not Italian. If you want the taste of Italian sauce, leave out the pepper and the water.
IT WAS KINDA BLAND AND HAD A CANNED TOMATO TASTE. I PREFER TO ADD RED WINE, TOMATO PASTE, OREGANO AND OTHER SPICES. I LIKE MOST OF THE RECIPES YOU SHARE. THIS ONE NOT SO MUCH.
Love it .
I can't thank you enough for the foundation you provided for this sauce. Tinker a little how you will. Thank you so much.
Not orthentic.

I wanted to take a moment to thank Richard and Suzanne (wish I knew your last name) because I believe that sharing a recipe is a way to say, "I value you, I want to gift you with something I love" and as the recipient of that recipe, I ALWAYS, ALWAYS, ALWAYS write the name of the person on the recipe so that every time I make it I can say, "I'm thinking of you Richard and Suzanne and I thank you for this gift you've given me. I do that too with recipes that had been given to my mom (now deceased) and passed on to me. "from Mrs. Gadda to my mom"--When I make it I close my eyes and say, "Thank you Mrs. Gadda for tucking my mom under your wing and teaching her how to make this recipe and thanks mom for giving it to me." It's a way to be remembered long after you're gone. My mother-in-law was a fabulous cook, but she held onto her recipes/methods and kept them "her magic." She's gone now and there's nothing left of that magic to remember her by. Through the years of me talking about this, folks have told me they're doing it too--remembering recipes given to them and being more open about sharing their magic (but asking that their name always accompany their recipes and that the thought behind it be shared with others to keep the circle going).

no oregano, no red wine, no rosemary, no tomatoe paste, no pepper? I guess if you were looking for something that tastes like a canned sauce, well this would work. If you were looking for something that resembled marinara it's missing a lot of flavor
fabulous!!! only thing is it takes much longer to cook the water out. i let it cook for twice as long and it was still pretty watery for what im used to but definitely yummy!
Excellent recipe with fantastic flavour.
